instructions: At least 5 hours ahead, or the day before: in a big bowl, stir the tapioca starch, rice flour, arrowroot, sugar and salt together. Slowly whisk in the coconut milk until there are no dry clumps.
Pour the batter through a sieve into another bowl, then divide it into two equal portions.

Cut the pandan leaves into short pieces and blend them with one portion of the batter until the leaves are fine. Pour it through a sieve lined with a cloth, squeezing out all the liquid, into a bowl. You now have one green batter and one white batter.
Fill a steamer pot with water and bring it to a boil. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel. Oil an 8 inch (20 cm) square pan with the oil, set it in the steamer and heat it for 3 minutes.
Stir the green batter and pour in a thin layer, about 1/3 cup, tilting the pan to cover the bottom. Cover and steam for 5 minutes, until set.

Stir the white batter and pour a thin layer on top. Cover and steam for 5 minutes. Keep alternating green and white, stirring each batter before you pour and steaming each layer for 5 minutes. Aim for about 9 layers, ending with green.
Steam the last layer for 15 minutes. Carefully lift the pan out and let the cake cool completely, at least 4 hours.
Loosen the edges with an oiled knife and turn the cake out. Cut it into diamonds or squares with an oiled knife. Serve at room temperature.
Covered, it keeps at room temperature for 2 days.
advance_prep_notes: make it at least 5 hours ahead, since it has to cool completely before you cut it.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings, so the lead is Hungry in Thailand (5 from 2 votes), whose flour, starch, sugar and coconut milk ratios match Dessertcat's almost exactly. The method (a thin layer at a time, about 5 minutes each, 9 layers, the lid wrapped in a cloth, a final longer steam) follows Dessertcat. Messy Vegan Cook steams each layer for 12 to 15 minutes and uses jasmine water; that is left out. It is a long cook, but it is a make-ahead cake.
